item.content:encoded:
Supervisor of Elections, Ana Mataiciwa will appear on fijivillage Straight Talk With Vijay Narayan at 7pm tomorrow.

The show will focus on the state of preparedness of the Fijian Elections Office for the proposed national referendum on December 9th and the next general elections which has to be held by February 6th 2027, the nationwide voter registration underway, changes to the electoral laws and the impact on the voters and the country, and the impact of any drastic changes with two months to go for the last day for the Writ of Elections to be issued on December 24th 2026 amongst other issues.

You can watch the Straight Talk interview on our facebook page, TikTok, YouTube and Instagram accounts.

You can also check out the podcast, fijivillage Straight Talk With Vijay Narayan on Spotify and Apple podcasts.

item.title: Emergency water supplies reach Cikobia despite rough seas
item.description: The National Disaster Risk Management Office says the MLC Vatulawa is currently at Cikobia Island, but rough sea conditions have made it unsafe to offload the main water supply. Despite the challenging conditions, the crew has managed to deliver bottled drinking water, sanitary hampers and a 5,000-litre water tank to schools and villages on the island.
item.content:encoded:
The National Disaster Risk Management Office says the MLC Vatulawa is currently at Cikobia Island, but rough sea conditions have made it unsafe to offload the main water supply.

Despite the challenging conditions, the crew has managed to deliver bottled drinking water, sanitary hampers and a 5,000-litre water tank to schools and villages on the island.

The NDRMO says the assistance will help meet the immediate needs of families and communities while they await the main water delivery.

They say authorities are closely monitoring weather and sea conditions, and water carting operations will resume once it is safe to do so.

The NDRMO adds that the safety of residents and response teams remains its top priority.

item.title: Ba business owner questions timing of Constitution Amendment Bill ahead of elections
item.description: A Ba business owner has questioned why amendments to the Constitution are being considered so close to the next general election, saying concerns about the Constitution could have been addressed earlier. Making a submission to the Joint Committee on the Constitution (Amendment) Bill 2026 at the Ba Market Bure, 28-year-old Sevanaia Levuidali raised concerns about provisions allowing Parliament’s te
item.content:encoded:
A Ba business owner has questioned why amendments to the Constitution are being considered so close to the next general election, saying concerns about the Constitution could have been addressed earlier.

Making a submission to the Joint Committee on the Constitution (Amendment) Bill 2026 at the Ba Market Bure, 28-year-old Sevanaia Levuidali raised concerns about provisions allowing Parliament’s term to be extended by up to 12 months if a State of Emergency is declared towards the end of its term.

Levuidali questioned why the issue had not been addressed in 2023 or 2024, or after the last general election, if there were concerns about the existing constitutional arrangements.

Levuidali says constitutional provisions are important laws that will guide the country and should be carefully considered.

He also raised concerns about identity politics, stressing the importance of recognising all Fijians, including those of Indian descent, as part of the country’s development.

He acknowledged the contributions of Fijians of Indian descent to the economy and the country, saying their sacrifices and contributions should be recognised.

Levuidali says Fiji should remain united in its diversity, guided by tolerance, goodwill and understanding.

He also appealed to legal professionals advising the Prime Minister to consider the interests of Fijians and future generations when assessing the proposed amendments.

Levuidali urged members of the committee and those involved in the amendment process to consider the long-term implications of their decisions for the country.

Consultations on the Bill will be held at George Shiu Raj Hall in Rakiraki from 10am to midday and at Rakiraki Village Hall in Navutulevu from 4pm to 6pm today.

Consultations will be held at Wailotua Village Hall in Wainibuka from 10am to midday and at Korovou Primary School Hall from 3pm to 5pm on tomorrow.

item.title: Police remain tight-lipped on Nadi murder as 2 other bodies found within five days
item.description: Police are not revealing if anyone has been brought in for questioning for the murder of a Nadi woman who was found near a Nadi complex last Thursday. They say investigations into the Nadi murder and the man who was found floating in the Labasa River on Friday continue .
item.content:encoded:
Police are not revealing if anyone has been brought in for questioning for the murder of a Nadi woman who was found near a Nadi complex last Thursday.

They say investigations into the Nadi murder and the man who was found floating in the Labasa River on Friday continue .

Police informed fijivillage News yesterday that the Labasa man's death is yet to be classified, as a post-mortem examination has not been conducted.

This comes as a third body has been found with the span of a week, where another woman's body was found at Thurston Gardens in Suva on Friday night.

Police are seeking assistance from the public in identifying the iTaukei woman, believed to be aged between 30 and 40 years.

They say one of her identifying marks is a tattoo of the word 'Kadavu' on her right shoulder, with a leaf beneath it.

The discovery of three bodies within five days has raised serious questions about the circumstances surrounding the deaths.
